# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-10 (Extended v96)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring-Summer Year 3, dual settings)**: (1) Paris, le Petit-Picpus convent district—Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary within walled convent garden; (2) English provincial harbor towns and hill farms (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton) with multiple inhabitants engaged in seasonal activities. Key historical dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont; Pontmercy-Gillenormand marriage; King of Prussia visits as "Count de Ruppin"); 1817 (young Parisians' excursion; M. Gillenormand began frequenting Madame de T.'s salon twice weekly in Rue Férou); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest, trial, Valjean's self-revelation, Fantine's death, Valjean's escape)**; **December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment; December 26 return to Paris)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed); **Summer Year 2 (achieved sanctuary in convent)**; **Winter Year 2 (Mother Crucifixion died, funeral, vault burial)**; **Spring-Summer Year 3 (currently occurring)**. **Environmental conditions (Spring-Summer Year 3)**: roads rutted and puddled after thaw; frost silvered hedges; bees hummed in lavender; children chased hoops; bell for vespers rang thinly; light went early; smoke lay flat over fields. **Population movements (English locations)**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged; Luena packed trunk, moved Staveford to Dungate; Rozek Stenenridge followed within month; Volan Stenworth mended sleeve by window, said little. **Dunstead granary fire**: Ismira told Luena the fire was set on purpose (claim/rumor).

## Primary Locations

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (convent carriage gate). **Convent complex—three buildings**: (1) Great Convent (Bernardines-Benedictines nuns); (2) Boarding-school; (3) Little Convent (aged nuns of various orders). **Interior garden**: Vast oblong with poplar alley, forest trees, gnarled fruit-tree, vegetable beds, melon patch, old well, stone benches. **Chapel**: Window visible from garden. **Burial location**: Mother Crucifixion's vault beneath grand altar (concealed). **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient burial ground with Prefecture Permission for nightfall interments; grave-digger Father Mestienne (deceased); replaced by "little Father Lenoir."

**ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton; market towns with parsonages, forges, granaries, ovens, wells, lanes.

**GORBEAU HOVEL (50-52)**: Salpêtrière district, outskirts Paris. Posted "Chambers to let"; presently inhabited by indigent individuals. **Current tenant—Jondrette family**: Father hired chamber, stated name upon hiring; instructed portress to respond affirmatively if inquired for Pole, Italian, or Spaniard.

**M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: **Rue Boucherat, Rue de Normandie, Rue de Saintonge** (ancient residents remember him); formerly **Rue Servandoni**; currently maintains **Rue Férou residence**. Doors absolutely closed during day; never receives anyone except evening; dines at five o'clock; after that door opens. Philosophy: "Day is vulgar. Fashionable people only light up minds when zenith lights stars."

**MADAME DE T.'S SALON (Rue Férou house)**: **Madame la Baronne de T.**, worthy respectable person; husband Baron de T. was Ambassador of France to Berlin under Louis XVI (died bankrupt during emigration, left ten manuscript volumes red morocco memoirs about Mesmer). Madame de T. maintains herself on meagre surviving income; lives in "very mixed society," noble isolation, proud and poor. Purely Royalist salon; few friends assemble twice weekly; sip tea; utter horror at century, charter, Bonapartists; speak low tones of hopes from Monsieur (Charles X); draw lists of chamber of peers; parodied Revolution; sang _Ça ira_. **Two cocks**: M. Gillenormand and Comte de Lamothe-Valois (of infamous necklace affair). **Society description**: essence and quintessence of Parisian white society; Royalist reputations held in quarantine; always trace of anarchy in renown; Chateaubriand would produce effect of Père Duchêne; some scoffed-at penetrated on sufferance. **Salon manners**: superior taste, exquisite and haughty under great show of politeness. Old régime habits, especially in language, seem eccentric. Titles: _Madame la Générale_, _Madame la Colonelle_ (Madame de Léon preferred this; Marquise de Créquy also called _Madame la Colonelle_).

## Jean Valjean's Psychological and Spiritual Development

**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank; understood contracting to fit diameter; could economize breath for hours without dying; possessed composure and coolness contagious to others.

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring-Summer Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works daily; formerly pruner of trees; knows agricultural secrets; budded ungrafted orchard trees producing excellent fruit. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running/playing; distinguishes her laugh.

**SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION**: During night meditations rose to listen to grateful song of innocent nuns; blood ran cold—justly chastised raised voices only in blasphemy while he, wretch, had shaken fist at God. Realized: scaling wall made to escape other place of expiation now served entrance to this one. Pride vanished. Scrutinized own heart; felt pettiness; wept many times. All entering life last six months led back towards Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Sometimes at eventide knelt in middle of walk skirting chapel, prostrated in prayer. Everything surrounding him—peaceful garden, fragrant flowers, children's joyous cries, grave and simple women, silent cloister—slowly permeated him. Soul became compounded of silence, perfume, simplicity, joy. Reflected: two houses of God received him at critical moments—first when all doors closed (society rejected him); second when society pursued him (galleys yawning). Without first, relapsed into crime; without second, into torment.

## Cosette's Integration and Development

**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Unhappiness trained her to silence. Hardly begun regaining confidence since with Jean Valjean.

**CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed; only regretted Catherine but dared not say so. Once told Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself his daughter. Became convent scholar; received pupil garb. Valjean succeeded getting nuns restore mourning suit from Thénardier departure; locked up these garments plus stockings/shoes with camphor/aromatics in little valise; procured valise, set on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Current Status

**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour traversing short distances; complains aching back.

**EXECUTION OF PLANS**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket, left with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert. Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery. At cemetery, grave-digger Father Mestienne dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Grave-digger lost card. Fauchelevent found card, buried corpse, filled grave himself.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives good wine. Old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally/protector. Nuns do not suspect him; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit and Investigation Status

**REASSIGNMENT AND REACTIVATION**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), Javert attached to Paris police. Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence.

**REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **Escape from Mouffetard**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS** (Spring-Summer Year 3): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades.

## M. Gillenormand and His World

**IDENTITY AND CHARACTER**: Worthy man; worthy bourgeois whose "consideration was of absolutely first-rate quality." Had certain manner imposing, dignified, honest, lofty in bourgeois fashion; great age added venerable dishevelment. Uttered frequently "the sensible man" and "nature." Gave nature his own acceptation in chimney-corner satires. Took prizes at College of Moulins (crowned by Duc de Nivernais). Neither Convention, death of Louis XVI, Napoleon, Bourbon return erased this memory. Lived in ancient Parisian neighborhoods; now in Rue Férou. Frequented Madame de T.'s salon twice weekly (1817 onward).

**SOCIAL DOMINATION**: Received in aristocratic salons despite bourgeois birth. Had double measure of wit (born with him, then attributed to him); sought out and made much of. Never went anywhere except on condition of being chief person there. Domination in Royalist salons cost his self-respect nothing. Oracle everywhere. Said things which had genuine sparkle of old rock. **Example witticisms**: When King of Prussia visited Louis XVIII. as "Count de Ruppin," Gillenormand approved: "All kings who are not the King of France are provincial kings." When asked _Courrier Français_ editor's sentence, replied: "To be suspended." "_Sus_ is superfluous." Remarks found situation.

**TWO DAUGHTERS**: Came into world ten years apart; in youth bore little resemblance. **Youngest**: Charming soul turned towards light, occupied with flowers, verses, music, fluttered into glorious space, enthusiastic, ethereal; wedded from youth in ideal to vague heroic figure; died 1815, leaving child. **Eldest** (Mademoiselle Gillenormand, the elder): Espied in azure wealthy purveyor/prefect ideal. Over forty, looked fifty; antique virtue, incombustible prude; one of sharpest noses and most obtuse minds. Outside immediate family, no one knew first name. Age accentuated pitiless modesty; guimpe never sufficiently opaque; multiplied clasps/pins. Peculiarity of prudery: place more sentinels as fortress less menaced. To prudery added bigotry. Belonged to society of Virgin; wore white veil on festivals; revered "holy blood," venerated "sacred heart"; remained hours contemplating rococo-jesuit altar. Chapel friend: ancient virgin Mademoiselle Vaubois (positive blockhead); beyond Agnus Dei/Ave Maria, knew nothing except preserves-making. Ermine of stupidity without single spot intelligence. Never malicious (relative kindness); years wore away angles; softening came. Melancholy with obscure sadness. Breathed from whole person stupor of life finished, never had beginning. Kept house for father; household of old man and old spinster touching aspect of two weaknesses leaning for support.

## Marius Pontmercy: Background and Current Status

**PARENTAGE AND EARLY YEARS**: Son of Colonel Pontmercy (chief of squadron, meagre half-pay); mother Madame Pontmercy (née Gillenormand, youngest daughter—"admirable woman in every sense, lofty in sentiment and rare"). **1815**: Pontmercy married Mademoiselle Gillenormand between two wars (during Empire); old M. Gillenormand gave consent with sigh, saying "Greatest families forced into it." Mother died 1815, leaving child. Colonel's joy in solitude; grandfather imperatively claimed grandson, declaring if child not given to him would disinherit. Father yielded in child's interest; transferred his love to flowers. Colonel lives alone at Vernon (smallest house he could find); has meagre half-pay as chief of squadron.

**CURRENT STATUS AND EDUCATION** (Age 7, Spring-Summer Year 3): Grandfather M. Gillenormand keeps up no relations with son-in-law (colonel "a bandit" to him); colonel called "brigand of the Loire." Never mentioned except with mocking allusions to "his Baronship." **Expressly agreed**: Pontmercy never attempt to see or speak to son under penalty of disinheritance. For Gillenormands, Pontmercy man afflicted with plague. Intended to bring up child in own way. Colonel wrong perhaps to accept conditions, but submitted, thinking he did right, sacrificing no one but himself.

**INHERITANCE**: Father Gillenormand's inheritance did not amount to much; but Mademoiselle Gillenormand the elder's inheritance considerable. This aunt, unmarried, very rich on maternal side; boy's natural heir. Boy's name Marius; knew he had father but nothing more. No one opened mouth to him about it. Nevertheless, in society grandfather took him, whispers, innuendoes, winks eventually enlightened Marius's mind; gradually understood case; by infiltration and slow penetration, came to think of father only with shame and pain at heart.

**SECRET PATERNAL VISITS**: Colonel slipped away every two or three months, came to Paris on sly, like criminal breaking ban, posted himself at Saint-Sulpice at hour when Aunt Gillenormand led Marius to mass. There, trembling lest aunt turn round, concealed behind pillar, motionless, not daring breathe, gazed at child. Scarred veteran afraid of old spinster.

**CORRESPONDENCE**: Twice yearly, first of January and St. George's day, Marius wrote duty letters to father, dictated by aunt, pronounced copied from formula. This all M. Gillenormand tolerated; father answered with very tender letters which grandfather thrust into pocket unread.

## Narrative Themes and Authorial Commentary

**AUDACITY AND REVOLUTION**: All sublime conquests are prizes of daring. For Revolution to take place, insufficient that Montesquieu foresee, Diderot preach, Beaumarchais announce, Condorcet calculate, Arouet prepare, Rousseau premeditate; necessary that Danton dare. Cry "Audacity!" is "Fiat lux." Necessary for forward march that proud lessons of courage permanently on heights. Daring deeds dazzle history.

**BOURGEOIS HONOR AND SOCIAL POSITION**: In bourgeoisie, honored situations decay through too easy relations; one must beware whom one admits. Loss of caloric in vicinity of cold mirrors diminution of consideration in approach of despised persons. Ancient upper-class society held above this law as above every other. Marigny (brother of Pompadour) had entry with M. le Prince de Soubise. Du Barry (god-father of Vaubernier) very welcome at M. le Maréchal de Richelieu's. That society is Olympus. Mercury and Prince de Guémenée at home there. A thief admitted, provided he be god.
